incidents.victim: US/Canada medical, academic & military research institutions
incidents.vector: Exploited externally facing REDCap research servers, deployed custom INFINITERED malware to steal credentials, then pivoted to domain admin and abused email content-compliance rules to silently exfiltrate data.
incidents.impact: A China-nexus actor (tracked as UNC6508) spied undetected for over a year, stealing credentials and sensitive research on AI, defense technology, military readiness and medicine; Google believes known victims are only a fraction of the campaign.

incidents.victim: Awesome Motive WordPress plugin users (~1.2M sites)
incidents.vector: Malicious code was injected into legitimate JavaScript of three popular plugins (OptinMonster, TrustPulse, PushEngage); it waits for an admin login, creates a rogue admin account and installs a hidden backdoor plugin.
incidents.impact: More than 1.2 million WordPress websites were backdoored following a compromise at plugin developer Awesome Motive, granting attackers persistent administrative access.

incidents.vector: Undisclosed intrusion that forced the company to take services offline; Astral is conducting a security review before restoring each service and Russian government agencies are involved in the investigation.
incidents.impact: A cyberattack disrupted Astral's tax-reporting, e-document and authentication services for about a week, affecting cash registers, customer portals, corporate email and HR systems at customers including Russian Post and Moscow transit operator Mosgortrans.

incidents.victim: Polish government officials, journalists & their families
incidents.vector: Credential-harvesting phishing pages, served from new domains almost daily, designed to steal Gmail logins and two-factor codes; attackers sometimes guess likely Gmail addresses of targets.
incidents.impact: Belarus-linked GhostWriter (UNC1151/Storm-0257) expanded operations to personal Gmail accounts of senior Polish public figures and relatives since March, seeking contacts, documents and linked accounts to enable further targeting and influence operations.

incidents.vector: Intruders gained access to parts of the company's internal network; Novo Nordisk took affected systems offline to investigate and evict the attackers.
incidents.impact: The maker of Ozempic and Wegovy disclosed that hackers accessed internal systems and copied some sensitive data, including patient personally identifiable information.

incidents.vector: Attackers allegedly compromised a developer laptop and stole private multisig keys, which were used to drain platform assets.
incidents.impact: About $36 million in crypto-assets were stolen and the Humanity token lost nearly 90% of its value shortly after the hack.

incidents.vector: Attackers abused an AUR mechanism to 'adopt' orphaned (abandoned) packages, then modified install procedures to pull a malicious npm package (later a Bun script) that installed a rootkit and infostealer.
incidents.impact: More than 1,900 Arch Linux AUR packages were hijacked over a weekend to deploy a rootkit and a credential/secret stealer targeting browsers, Electron apps and developer keys; affected users were urged to rotate all credentials.

incidents.victim: Universities, Council of Europe, Ralph Lauren, JCPenney, Nexstar
incidents.vector: Exploitation of an Oracle PeopleSoft ERP zero-day (CVE-2026-35273, added to CISA's KEV catalog) to steal large volumes of records, followed by extortion demands.
incidents.impact: ShinyHunters listed a new batch of extortion victims; the University of Nottingham alone reported 40GB of data and records for 450,000+ students and alumni stolen from its PeopleSoft platform.

incidents.vector: Conti operators hacked into victim networks, encrypted data and demanded ransom to restore access and prevent leak of stolen data; the defendant coded a malware 'loader.'
incidents.impact: Ukrainian national Oleksii Lytvynenko pleaded guilty to wire-fraud conspiracy after extradition from Ireland; Conti infected 1,000+ networks across 47 US states and 31 countries and caused at least $150M in ransom payments.

incidents.vector: Data allegedly stolen from a government agency managing healthcare entitlements; some records subsequently posted on online black markets.
incidents.impact: Hackers allegedly stole the personal information of more than 67 million Thai citizens; the Thai government has launched an investigation.

incidents.vector: Compromise of the lawmaker's Signal messaging account; the FBI notified him of the breach.
incidents.impact: Suspected Russian hackers breached the Signal account of Rep. Don Bacon, a vocal supporter of Ukraine and critic of the Kremlin.

incidents.victim: US security-clearance holders & former government employees
incidents.vector: At least 13 fake consulting-company websites with AI-generated photos and stolen identities lured cleared personnel via job platforms, paying for 'research reports' to extract insider and classified information.
incidents.impact: The DOJ and FBI seized 13 domains used by suspected Chinese intelligence to recruit current and former US clearance holders; takeover pages were placed to disrupt the scheme.

incidents.victim: Organizations running Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of an improper output encoding/escaping zero-day in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager (CVE-2026-20245), added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
incidents.impact: Cisco customers faced another SD-WAN zero-day under active attack; CISA ordered rapid federal remediation, with some KEV deadlines now as short as three days.

incidents.victim: Organizations running Check Point Security Gateways
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of an improper-authentication zero-day in Check Point Security Gateway VPN/remote-access products (CVE-2026-50751), added to CISA's KEV catalog.
incidents.impact: The Qilin ransomware operation exploited a Check Point VPN/gateway flaw used as a network gatekeeper; CISA gave US federal agencies three days to patch.

incidents.vector: A variant of the self-spreading Shai-Hulud worm infected packages tied to Microsoft's official Azure Durable Task SDK, propagating across repositories and harvesting credentials.
incidents.impact: At least 72 of Microsoft's public code repositories were infected with the Shai-Hulud worm, the second time the SDK was hit by the worm in as many months.

incidents.vector: A spear-phishing operation tried to lure WhatsApp users into clicking a malicious link leading to an external site, in violation of a US court injunction.
incidents.impact: Meta says it disrupted a new NSO Group campaign targeting WhatsApp users and filed to hold the sanctioned spyware maker in contempt of court.

incidents.victim: Obama White House & US Space Force Instagram accounts
incidents.vector: Attackers tricked Meta's AI support assistant into adding an attacker email to target accounts (using a VPN IP near the target's hometown), triggering a one-time code that enabled password resets.
incidents.impact: High-profile Instagram accounts were briefly defaced with pro-Iranian images and messages; Meta issued an emergency patch and said no back-end database was breached.

incidents.victim: EU targets of Russian cyber & influence operations
incidents.vector: Dutch financial-crime investigators arrested the co-owners of hosting firms (MIRhosting/WorkTitans) that took over Stark Industries' infrastructure used to stage DDoS, cyber and disinformation operations for Russia.
incidents.impact: Two men were arrested and over 800 servers seized; the hosting was the most-used network in pro-Russian attacks on Danish government bodies during Denmark's November 2025 municipal elections.
